description: We are a team of enthusiasts from Cherkasy.
summary: We built Igris to help people find and understand NASA research on combustion in microgravity. The results are spread across experiment records, publications and data files, so finding a useful answer takes more than a keyword search. Igris brings a searchable catalog, an AI assistant and study comparisons into one place. Users can ask questions in English or Ukrainian and follow the sources behind an answer. The assistant searches our knowledge base and consults NASA NTRS when needed. For the Flame in Freefall challenge, our focus is helping researchers, engineers and students explore combustion evidence and identify gaps relevant to fire safety. The working demo uses NASA PSI records, selected indexed files and scientific reports.
details:
The data exists. The answers are hard to find. We built Igris around this problem.

Ask, find, compare

Users can ask questions in English or Ukrainian, browse investigations by topic, hardware and data availability, or compare studies. The catalog brings together experiment objectives, methods, publications and links to original files. Analytics provides an overview of the catalog.

How it works

The assistant uses the question and conversation context to retrieve NASA PSI records, publications and indexed file excerpts from our knowledge base. When needed, it searches NASA NTRS for reports, abstracts and available text. It explains the findings with source references and identifies missing evidence. Igris validates source references and applies additional evidence review to comparisons, detailed data questions and live NASA results.

Who it helps

Our focus is combustion in microgravity and research relevant to spacecraft fire safety. We want researchers to spend less time searching and more time examining evidence. Engineers can find material for further analysis, while students and teachers can explore complex studies through explanations with original sources. The demo indexes a subset of open PSI files. Any use in safety decisions requires further scientific review.

Tools and development

We used TypeScript, Next.js and React, with Astryx for the interface, Supabase/PostgreSQL for storage and search, and Render for hosting. AI through the Radium API plans searches and drafts answers from retrieved sources. Claude (Anthropic) and Codex (OpenAI) assisted with development and presentation preparation under our team's direction and review. Research data comes from the cited sources.

Next, we plan to expand the searchable material and file index, improve retrieval and answer review, and scale the service. Igris also supports other areas of NASA physical-science research.
